Proceedings of the 37 th International Conference on Machine Learning, Vienna, Austria, PMLR 119, 2020.

contribution.value: AdaRound is a post-training weight-rounding method that adapts to data and task loss using a per-layer QUBO formulation solved via continuous relaxation, quantizing ResNet-18/50 weights to 4 bits within 1% accuracy drop.

ev.quote: we propose AdaRound, a better weight-rounding mechanism for post-training quantization that adapts to the data and the task loss. AdaRound is fast, does not require finetuning of the network, and only uses a small amount of unlabelled data.

we report the mean and standard deviation of the (top1) accuracy on the ImageNet validation set, calculated using 5 runs with different initial seeds. To optimize AdaRound we use 1024 unlabeled images from the ImageNet (Russakovsky et al., 2015) training set
we apply it to DeeplabV3+ (Chen et al., 2018) evaluated on Pascal VOC (Everingham et al., 2015). Since the input images here are significantly bigger, we only use 512 images to optimize AdaRound.

strengths.value: Recovers ResNet-18 and ResNet-50 4-bit weight accuracy to within 1% of FP32, a clear new state-of-the-art for PTQ.

ev.quote: Without fine-tuning, we can quantize the weights of Resnet18 and Resnet50 to 4 bits while staying within an accuracy loss of 1%.

strengths.value: Computationally fast: AdaRound on ResNet-18 finishes in 10 minutes on one GTX 1080 Ti.

ev.quote: the application of AdaRound to Resnet18 takes only 10 minutes on a single Nvidia GTX 1080 Ti.

strengths.value: Robust to calibration data: as few as 256 unlabeled images, even from out-of-distribution sets, recover within ~2% of FP32.

ev.quote: Even with as little as 256 images, the method optimizes the model to within 2% of the original FP32 accuracy. We also see that when using unlabelled images that are from a similar domain but do not belong to the original training data, AdaRound achieves competitive performance.

strengths.value: Theoretically grounded: derives the rounding objective from a Taylor expansion of the task loss into a per-layer QUBO.

ev.quote: We establish a theoretical framework to analyze the effect of rounding ... we formulate rounding as a perlayer Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization (QUBO) problem.

weaknesses.value: Step size and rounding are not jointly optimised; any change to step size produces a different QUBO problem.

ev.quote: we do not optimize step size and AdaRound jointly as it is non-trivial to combine the two tasks: any change in the step size would result in a different QUBO problem.

weaknesses.value: The diagonal preactivation Hessian is an approximation; ignoring cross-layer interactions and treating diag entries as constant is a simplification.

ev.section: 3.2. From Taylor expansion to local loss
ev.quote: we make the assumption that the Hessian of the task loss w.r.t. the preactivations, i.e., \nabla^2_{\mathbf{z}^{(\ell)}} \mathcal{L} is a diagonal matrix

weaknesses.value: Activation quantization uses only simple min-max scaling, which limits aggressiveness on activations.

ev.quote: we quantized the activations to 8 bits and set the scaling factor for the activation quantizers based on the minimum and maximum activations observed.

limitations.value: Validated only on CNN computer-vision models (ResNet, Inception, MobileNetV2, DeepLabV3+); transformers and language models are not evaluated.

ev.quote: we conduct experiments on various computer vision tasks and models.

limitations.value: Lowest weight bitwidth tested is 4; sub-4-bit (3-bit, 2-bit) regimes are not explored in the main experiments.

ev.quote: We use symmetric 4-bit weight quantization with a per-layer scale parameter s^{(\ell)} which is determined prior to the application of AdaRound.

limitations.value: Activation quantization is limited to 8 bits; activations below 8 bits are not investigated.

ev.quote: we report results of AdaRound with all activation tensors quantized to 8 bits.

limitations.value: No measurement of real inference latency, throughput, or energy on edge hardware; all reported runtimes are calibration cost on a desktop GPU.

ev.quote: the application of AdaRound to Resnet18 takes only 10 minutes on a single Nvidia GTX 1080 Ti.

future_work_stated.value: Combine AdaRound with mixed-precision PTQ methods (HAWQ, ZeroQ) and channel-splitting (OCS) to push lower bits.
